basis: scripts/reference_provenance.json; committed source and paper text only

classification.caveat: README:178 states the head fires on any close surface, including hood walls and the arm's own links, which is precisely why the demos subtract. Used raw inside a fumehood cavity it would push constantly. Its behaviour there has never been measured.
classification.label: DEPLOYABLE
classification.why: Needs only the live 40-sensor reading. It is also the ONLY option whose input distribution matches Safety-CVAE training, which used raw absolute depths with no subtraction anywhere (train_safety_cvae.py:2-3, 89-94).

classification.caveat: Not equivalent to the documented parked-obstacle subtraction. The one completed pair shows why: the reference is frozen at the step-0 posture while active sensors grow 10 -> 22 as the arm enters the cavity, so the residual tracks posture drift rather than hazard proximity (see one_pair_attribution.json).
classification.label: NOVEL_UNVALIDATED
classification.why: Deployable, but established by nothing: it appears in no README passage, no committed demo and no paper text, existing only as the else-branch at eval_act_obstacle_safety.py:213-215.

classification.caveat: Requires rendering a hazard-free scene, and does not transfer to a moving arm.
classification.label: HISTORICAL_DEMO_ONLY
classification.why: Used by safety_flinch_demo.py:293-296, where a single baseline is valid only because the arm is held at a fixed rest posture (lines 85, 109).

classification.caveat: Requires privileged mocap manipulation and a second render per frame. Sound as an oracle upper bound; not deployable on hardware.
classification.label: SIMULATION_ORACLE
classification.why: THE documented canonical contract: README:174 and safety_react_demo.py:368-379, which parks the bars at the CURRENT pose, re-renders, subtracts and restores, every frame.

classification.caveat: Self-defeating for a residual controller: the moment the residual makes ACT deviate -- its entire purpose -- the reference describes a posture the robot is no longer in. It also needs a paired pre-recorded episode, so it is privileged as well.
classification.label: UNSUPPORTED
classification.why: Available at eval_act_obstacle_safety.py:206-212 via --baseline_reference_h5, but it is indexed by step, so it is frame-aligned only while the live rollout still tracks the recorded trajectory.

important_distinctions.first_live_is_not_the_documented_subtrac: A frozen first-live reference is deployable but is not automatically equivalent to the documented parked-obstacle subtraction, and the measured one-pair behaviour shows the two are materially different.
important_distinctions.oracle_vs_deployable: A frame-aligned obstacle-parked or obstacle-removed reference is useful as a simulation oracle but uses privileged counterfactual information, so results obtained with it cannot be presented as achievable on hardware.
important_distinctions.react_demo_does_not_transfer: The recorded-trajectory react demo does not by itself prove the same baseline works for a live, deviating ACT rollout: the demo recomputes its baseline per-frame at the current pose, so it never relies on posture agreement with a recording.

principle: The project's canonical implementation requires privileged counterfactual information, so no non-privileged reference is established as the intended live controller. This task therefore classifies the options and escalates rather than choosing one.
recommendation_withheld: Not chosen here. Selecting among A-D changes what the safety result means scientifically, so it belongs to whoever owns the claim, not to this repair task.
